[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Configuration Tuning (postgresql.conf for Production)"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The default configuration file (postgresql.conf) shipped with PostgreSQL is designed to run on almost any system with minimal resource consumption. For production environments, these settings must be tuned to leverage the available system memory, CPU cores, and disk I/O capabilities to prevent bottlenecks and ensure stability."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Memory Allocation Parameters"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Memory tuning is the most critical aspect of PostgreSQL performance optimization. The following parameters dictate how PostgreSQL utilizes system RAM:"},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"shared_buffers: Determines how much dedicated memory PostgreSQL uses for caching data. For production servers, set this to approximately 25% of total system RAM."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"work_mem: Specifies the amount of memory used by internal sort operations and hash tables before writing to temporary disk files. This is allocated per-query, per-operation, so setting it too high can exhaust RAM under high concurrency."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"maintenance_work_mem: Specifies the maximum amount of memory to be used by maintenance operations, such as VACUUM, CREATE INDEX, and ALTER TABLE. Set this significantly higher than work_mem (e.g., 1GB to 2GB on modern systems)."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"effective_cache_size: An estimate of how much memory is available for disk caching by both the operating system and within PostgreSQL. Set this to roughly 50% to 75% of total system RAM."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"# Memory Settings for a 16GB RAM Server
shared_buffers = 4GB
work_mem = 64MB
maintenance_work_mem = 1GB
effective_cache_size = 12GB"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Write-Ahead Log (WAL) and Checkpoints"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Checkpoints are points in the transaction log sequence at which all data files are updated to reflect the information in the WAL. Tuning checkpoints reduces disk write spikes and improves overall write throughput."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"max_wal_size: The maximum size to let the WAL grow during checkpoints. Setting this to a higher value (e.g., 16GB to 32GB) reduces checkpoint frequency and write amplification."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"checkpoint_timeout: The maximum time between automatic WAL checkpoints. Increasing this from the default 5 minutes to 15 or 30 minutes improves performance at the cost of longer recovery times during a crash."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"checkpoint_completion_target: Specifies the target of checkpoint completion, as a fraction of total time between checkpoints. The recommended value is 0.9, which spreads the writes evenly across 90% of the checkpoint interval."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"# WAL and Checkpoint Settings
wal_buffers = 16MB
checkpoint_timeout = 15min
checkpoint_completion_target = 0.9
max_wal_size = 16GB
min_wal_size = 2GB"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Connections and Parallel Workers"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Managing connections and parallel execution is vital to prevent CPU thrashing and memory exhaustion."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"max_connections: The maximum number of concurrent client connections. Setting this too high (e.g., > 500) degrades performance due to connection overhead. Use a connection pooler like PgBouncer for high-concurrency workloads."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"max_worker_processes: Sets the maximum number of background processes that the system can support. This should match the number of available CPU cores."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"max_parallel_workers_per_gather: Sets the maximum number of workers that can be started by a single 'Gather' or 'Gather Merge' node. Usually set to 2 to 4 depending on core count."},{"order":21,"type":"code","text":"# Connection and Worker Settings
max_connections = 100
max_worker_processes = 8
max_parallel_workers_per_gather = 2
max_parallel_workers = 8"},{"order":22,"type":"subheading","text":"Applying Configuration Changes"},{"order":23,"type":"paragraph","text":"Some configuration parameters can be reloaded dynamically without restarting the database server, while others require a full restart. You can check which parameters require a restart by querying the pg_settings system view."},{"order":24,"type":"code","text":"-- Reload configuration without restarting the service
SELECT pg_reload_conf();

-- Query to check which parameters require a restart to take effect
SELECT name, setting, context 
FROM pg_settings 
WHERE context = 'postmaster';"}]
